root_cause.text: AppArmor policy namespace creation in `__aa_create_ns()` had no explicit nesting-depth limit, so attackers could create arbitrarily deep `aa_ns` hierarchies and exhaust system resources because the code relied on user-namespace limits that do not bound policy namespaces.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE text says policy namespaces “aren't strictly tied to user namespaces” and “it is possible to create them and nest them arbitrarily deep,” and the patch adds `MAX_NS_DEPTH 32` plus `if (parent->level > MAX_NS_DEPTH) return ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC);` in `security/apparmor/policy_ns.c` to enforce a hard cap.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE text says policy namespaces “aren't strictly tied to user namespaces” and “it is possible to create them and nest them arbitrarily deep,” and the patch adds `MAX_NS_DEPTH 32` plus `if (parent->level > MAX_NS_DEPTH) return ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC);` in `security/apparmor/policy_ns.c` to enforce a hard cap.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a constant defining the maximum AppArmor namespace depth to match the user namespace limit.
intent_record.what: A new preprocessor macro `MAX_NS_DEPTH` is added with the value `32`, along with a comment stating it matches the maximum depth of user namespaces.
intent_record.how: This introduces a named constant that can be used elsewhere in the code to cap namespace nesting at 32 levels, aligning AppArmor namespace depth handling with the user namespace limit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a depth limit check to prevent creating namespaces beyond the maximum allowed nesting level.
intent_record.what: A new conditional check was added at the start of __aa_create_ns(): if parent->level is greater than MAX_NS_DEPTH, the function now returns ERR_PTR(-ENOSPC) before calling alloc_ns().
intent_record.how: This prevents creation of additional namespaces once the maximum namespace nesting depth has been exceeded, causing the function to fail early with -ENOSPC instead of attempting to allocate a deeper namespace.

Add a depth limit check to prevent creating namespaces beyond the maximum allowed nesting level.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by introducing an explicit maximum AppArmor namespace nesting depth, which prevents arbitrarily deep aa_ns hierarchies and the resulting resource exhaustion.
The change directly matches the root cause: it adds an explicit nesting-depth limit to AppArmor namespace creation, preventing arbitrarily deep aa_ns hierarchies and resource exhaustion.

candidates.rationale: This is the namespace creation point in __aa_create_ns(); before the fix there was no depth check guarding this allocation, so repeated calls could create arbitrarily deep AppArmor namespace hierarchies.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the namespace allocation in __aa_create_ns() that occurred before any explicit nesting-depth validation. Without a depth limit check, repeated invocations could create arbitrarily deep AppArmor namespace hierarchies and exhaust resources.
